outcome: No result since 26 January 2024 settles termination of flips in every dimension above 3; in that window there are one conditional flips-with-scaling result in any dimension (Kim, May 2024), one dimension-3 result in positive characteristic (Yang-Ye-Zhang, Aug 2024), a dimension-5 termination result for big general-type MMPs (Han-Liu-Zhuang, Sep 2025), and OpenAI manuscripts of 24 Sep and 7 Oct 2026 that prove termination in dimension 4 for projective log canonical fourfolds with rational boundary and for generalized log canonical flips on compact Kähler fourfolds, both produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model and with no outside review I could find.
problem_asks: Read as the bullet gives it, the question has these parts. (1) Dimensions: 'dimensions greater than 3' means every dimension n >= 4, so the answer must cover n = 4, n = 5, and all higher n, not just one of them. (2) Objects: 'infinite sequences of flips' is the termination conjecture, that every sequence of flips terminates after finitely many steps. The bullet does not restrict the class of flips. The Wikipedia Flip article's footnote states the conjecture for flips of klt varieties, projective over a fixed normal variety; the bullet's wording and the article's footnote therefore differ in scope and both are recorded. (3) Existence of flips is a separate question in the article's framing ('two major problems') and is not asked by this bullet. (4) An answer of 'no' in a class of pairs (klt, lc, generalized, Kähler, rational boundary, big boundary, scaling) covers only that class; the bullet asks about all flips in all dimensions above 3.

events.what_happened: Fujino, 'Termination of 4-fold canonical flips', arXiv math/0301154 (one version). The abstract reads 'We prove the termination of 4-fold canonical flips.' The comments say it is a revised version of a private note circulated in May 2002. The addendum (event fujino-2004-canonical-addendum) says the weighted difficulty in this paper contains errors.

events.delivers: Per the abstract, termination of every sequence of canonical flips in dimension 4. The abstract gives no hypotheses beyond 'canonical'. The addendum says the argument's difficulty function was defined incorrectly, so the claim is not relied on without the corrected statement in the addendum.
events.remains: Dimensions 5 and above. Dimension-4 flips outside the canonical class (non-canonical, log, klt).

events.what_happened: Birkar, 'ACC for log canonical thresholds and termination of log flips', arXiv math/0502116 (one version, 6 Feb 2005). Abstract (opened): ACC for log canonical thresholds in dimension d together with special termination in dimension d implies termination of any sequence of log flips starting from a d-dimensional lc pair of nonnegative Kodaira dimension. It also notes that in characteristic zero, termination in dimension 4 would follow from Alexeev-Borisov's conjecture in dimension 3.
events.delivers: A conditional reduction: termination of log flips in dimension d for lc pairs of nonnegative Kodaira dimension, given ACC for lc thresholds and special termination in dimension d.
events.remains: The two hypotheses in each dimension; unconditional termination in any dimension.
events.direction: A reduction in the termination direction; no unconditional claim.

Abstract (opened): termination of 4-dimensional log flips starting from a klt pair (X,D) where -(K+D) is numerically equivalent to an effective divisor; also log Fano pairs, relative birational settings, and directed flips with K+D big. Listed consequences include existence of 5-dimensional log flips and minimal models for 4-dimensional dlt pairs of general type.
events.delivers: Termination of 4-dimensional log flips starting from a klt pair with -(K+D) numerically effective, together with the log Fano, relative and directed-with-big-K+D cases named in the abstract.
events.remains: 4-dimensional log flips without the numerical condition, outside the directed case; dimensions 5 and above.

events.what_happened: Han, Liu, Zhuang, 'Effective termination of general type MMPs in dimension at most five', arXiv 2509.01501 (one version, 1 Sep 2025; a companion to arXiv:2506.20183). Theorem 1.1 (opened, HTML): for a projective klt pair (X,Delta) of dimension 5 with K+Delta big, or K+Delta pseudo-effective and Delta big, there is an m depending on (X,Delta) such that every (K+Delta)-MMP terminates after at most m steps; m is not given explicitly. events.doubts: The step bound is non-explicit, so the dimension-5 statement is ineffective. This is a feature of the statement rather than a doubt about it.
events.direction: Termination in a restricted class in dimension 5 (general type, big boundary); cuts toward the expected answer in that class.

events.what_happened: OpenAI, 'Termination for projective log canonical fourfolds with rational boundary', dated 24 Sep 2026 (family 056 of the release's manuscript map), at github.com/openai/math, preprints/Termination-for-projective-log-canonical-fourfolds-with-rational-boundary-September-24-2026/. Abstract (opened, paper.tex): 'every permitted minimal model program for a projective log canonical fourfold with rational boundary over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero terminates', allowing arbitrary negative extremal rays and mixed birational steps, and needing no pseudo-effectivity or initial Q-factoriality. Main theorem (opened, introduction): (i) every negative extremal ray at every stage has a contraction and, when birational, a positive model; (ii) every program starting from (X,B) has finitely many birational steps, for every sequence of permitted choices; (iii) every maximal program ends either at a projective lc pair with nef adjoint or at a Mori fibre space. The introduction calls it 'the projective four-dimensional case of the Termination of Flips Conjecture.' Author line: 'OpenAI'. The release README says the manuscripts were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model.
events.revisions: None found beyond the 24 Sep 2026 version.
events.delivers: Termination of every permitted MMP for projective lc 4-folds with rational boundary, in characteristic zero, without pseudo-effectivity or Q-factoriality (per the abstract and the introduction's main theorem). Dimension 4 only.
events.remains: Every dimension other than 4; Kähler (non-projective) pairs; non-rational boundary. 'Permitted' is defined in sections I did not read, so the exact class of programs covered is not established.
events.doubts: (1) Unrefereed, AI-produced manuscript per the release README; no outside reader found. (2) 'Permitted' is defined in sections not read, so the class of MMPs covered is not confirmed. (3) The release README reports three manuscripts withdrawn on 7 Oct 2026 for a sign error in a Weil-classes / K3 Hodge argument; their titles are not MMP work, so this does not directly touch this manuscript. (4) The paper cites OpenAI companion manuscripts for endpoint consequences (OpenAILogAbundance2026, OpenAIComplements2026, OpenAICartier2026), and says 'The termination proof is independent of the companion results used for the endpoint consequences.' A third-party site flagged an apparent conflict between two OpenAI log-abundance manuscripts (per a search extract, VibeMathed); that is not a termination statement. (5) No Lean entry for this manuscript in lean/formalization.yaml.
events.direction: Termination in its class (dimension 4, projective lc, rational boundary); cuts toward the expected answer in that class.

events.what_happened: OpenAI, 'Termination of generalized log canonical flips on compact Kähler fourfolds', folder dated 7 Oct 2026 in preprints/, with LaTeX source build/termination-generalized-lc-kahler-fourfolds.tex (the tex date is 7 Oct 2026). The folder README links an Oct 5 version and says this version 'clarifies the independent relative MMP and birational-comparison inputs used by the proof' and 'updates citations to revised companion papers'. Abstract (opened, read in two chunks by a summarising fetch; quotes are that fetch's reproduction): 'Every sequence of generalized log canonical flips on a normal irreducible globally Weil Q-factorial compact Kähler fourfold terminates, provided the flips are projective small diagrams with the stated opposite ample signs.' 'The boundary is rational, and the nef b-divisor is fixed and represented by an analytically nef Q-Cartier divisor on a projective modification.' 'No scaling rule or pseudo-effectivity assumption is required.' 'The theorem concerns existing flip sequences; it does not assert the existence of all contractions or flips.' Main theorem (thm:main): a sequence X_i, each a normal irreducible globally Weil Q-factorial compact Kähler fourfold, with steps X_i -> Z_i <- X_{i+1} projective small bimeromorphic morphisms, neither an isomorphism, and sign conditions '-D_i is f_i-ample' and 'D_{i+1} is f_i^+-ample'; the conclusion is 'the sequence is finite'. Proof by contradiction via gdlt lifts, invoking thm:special-termination and thm:gdlt. Cites two companion OpenAI manuscripts: KahlerAuxiliary ('Finite ordinary minimal model programs on compact Kähler fourfolds') and ProjectiveLCFourfolds ('Termination for projective log canonical fourfolds with rational boundary'). The body also says it treats 'a four-dimensional special case' of a termination conjecture of Hacon and Xie for generalized klt pairs with higher (1,1)-class data on compact Kähler spaces.
events.revisions: An earlier version dated 5 Oct 2026 is linked from the folder README; this is the 7 Oct version. A history.md entry for the same day revised six 'Kähler minimal model programs and abundance' manuscripts ('expanded positivity and contraction arguments and clarified which results are used as inputs'); I could not tell from the text whether those include this manuscript.
events.delivers: Termination of every sequence of generalized log canonical flips on normal, irreducible, globally Weil Q-factorial compact Kähler 4-folds, provided each step is a projective small diagram with the stated opposite ample signs, the boundary is rational and the nef b-divisor is fixed; no scaling or pseudo-effectivity assumption. Dimension 4 only. It assumes the existence of the flip diagrams and does not prove it.
events.remains: Dimensions 5 and above, and dimension 3 for these pairs is not stated; existence of the diagrams (assumed); non-Kähler and non-generalized settings; the Hacon-Xie conjecture in general (the paper treats a 4-dimensional special case).
events.doubts: (1) Unrefereed, AI-produced manuscript per the release README; no human reader found. (2) It depends on two other OpenAI manuscripts that are also unrefereed (KahlerAuxiliary and ProjectiveLCFourfolds). The folder README says the version clarifies which inputs from the companion are used. (3) The input list changed within a day of release (folder README version note; the history.md entry for 7 Oct revised six related Kähler manuscripts). (4) The result is conditional on the existence of the flip diagrams, which the paper says it does not assert. (5) No Lean entry for this manuscript in lean/formalization.yaml, which records review status 'unchecked'.

events.what_happened: Five manuscripts, all about fourfolds, each claiming a termination result in dimension four. None treats dimension five or higher. (a) 'Termination of generalized log canonical flips on compact Kähler fourfolds' (October 7, 2026; main theorem thm:main): for a normal irreducible globally Weil Q-factorial compact Kähler fourfold X_0 with effective rational boundary B_0 of coefficients in [0,1], and a rational b-divisor represented by an analytically nef Q-Cartier divisor on a projective model, with (X_0, B_0+M) generalized log canonical, every sequence of flips X_i -> Z_i <- X_{i+1} (projective small maps with connected fibres, Z_i normal compact Kähler, neither map an isomorphism, -D_i f_i-ample, D_{i+1} f_i^+-ample) is finite. M=0 gives the ordinary lc case. (b) 'Termination of generalized-canonical flips on compact Kähler fourfolds' (October 6, 2026; build/build/paper.tex, theorem thm:termination): the same conclusion with boundary coefficients in [0,1) and generalized canonical hypotheses (every log discrepancy on X_0 positive, exceptional ones at least 1). (c) 'Termination for projective log canonical fourfolds with rational boundary' (September 24, 2026): for a projective lc fourfold with rational boundary over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, (i) every negative extremal ray has its contraction and, when birational, a positive model; (ii) every permitted program has finitely many birational steps for every choice of rays, where a permitted program steps by contracting a negative extremal ray of relative Picard number one, followed by a divisorial contraction, a projective small flip, or a mixed step; (iii) maximal programs end at a nef lc model or a Mori fibre space. No Q-factoriality or pseudo-effectivity is assumed. (d) 'Finite ordinary minimal model programs on compact Kähler fourfolds' (October 6, 2026; theorem thm:finite): for a normal globally Weil Q-factorial compact Kähler fourfold with klt effective rational boundary, every maximal program of ordinary negative steps (projective divisorial contractions and flips of D-negative extremal rays) terminates. The endpoint is nef when K+Δ is pseudo-effective, and otherwise a projective Mori fibre space over a base of dimension below four. Its finiteness of flip tails is taken from (a), via its Corollary repair:cor:existing. (e) 'Finite ordinary minimal model programs on compact Kähler fourfolds' (September 24, 2026; an earlier paper with the same title as (d)): for the same klt Kähler setting, there exists one finite ordinary program, obtained by a suitable choice of steps, with the same endpoint classification. It does not claim termination for every choice.
events.revisions: 3 earlier edition(s) kept in the repository: Termination-of-generalized-log-canonical-flips-on-compact-Kahler-fourfolds-October-5-2026, Termination-of-generalized-canonical-flips-on-compact-Kahler-fourfolds-October-5-2026, Finite-ordinary-minimal-model-programs-on-compact-Kahler-fourfolds-October-5-2026
events.delivers: Dimension four only, in the stated classes. (a) and (b) answer no for the flip sequences they describe: on Kähler, globally Weil Q-factorial fourfolds with a fixed rational nef b-divisor, no infinite sequence of such flips exists. They need no pseudo-effectivity or scaling, and the flips need not be extremal and the Z_i need not share a base. (c) answers no for every permitted program, hence for flips occurring as steps of such programs, on projective lc fourfolds with rational boundary, without Q-factoriality. Its singularity class is wider than (d)'s, but its flips must each contract a relative Picard number one extremal ray. (d) answers no for every maximal ordinary program on klt Kähler fourfolds: an infinite run would contain an infinite tail of flips, which (d) excludes by citing (a). Its divisorial steps are finite by a cycle count. (e) gives only existence of one finite program and says nothing about infinite sequences in general. The manuscripts do not claim to settle the bullet as the list words it. (c) says it proves 'the projective four-dimensional case of the Termination of Flips Conjecture for ordinary log canonical pairs with rational boundary'. (e) says it gives 'an affirmative solution of the finite-program form of the rational klt fourfold minimal model conjecture' in the Kähler category, and does not state that form. Against the bullet's parts: (1) dimensions: only n = 4 is treated; (2) objects: flips of pairs in the classes above, not all flips; (3) existence is not asked, but (a) and (b) state they do not assert existence of contractions or flips, while (c) and (d) construct the steps they use; (4) each 'no' covers only its class.
events.remains: If the claims hold, still open for this bullet: every dimension n >= 5. In dimension four: flip sequences outside the classes above, including non-Q-factorial ambients for (a), (b), (d) and (e); non-Kähler ambients or non-projective flips for (a) and (b); boundaries with coefficients outside [0,1], non-lc pairs for (c), and non-klt pairs for (d) and (e); varying nef data for (a) and (b); arbitrary flip sequences that are not programs in (c), (d) and (e); flips whose negative contraction has relative Picard number above one, in (c); existence of flips in (a) and (b); termination for every choice of steps in (e). No manuscript treats the footnote's class directly: klt flips, projective over one fixed normal base. None of them fixes a base, and (a), (b), (d) and (e) add Kähler and global Weil Q-factoriality hypotheses.
events.doubts: (1) (a) and (d) depend on each other: (d) uses (a)'s flip theorem for infinite flip tails, and (a) uses (d)'s special-termination and relative-program results. (d)'s Section 6 opening states that those results do not depend on its finite-program theorem. The loop is between papers, and that assertion is the one a reader must check. (2) (d)'s intrinsic formulation, with a canonical rational line bundle in place of a canonical divisor, is argued in one paragraph that ends 'leaves that proof unchanged'. (3) (b) says it 'reproduces these arguments in full and invokes no termination theorem', yet its negativity, terminal-smoothness and cycle-comparison inputs are cited to (e). (4) The introduction of (a) summarises its branch and difficulty estimates by method (Quot parameters, local factorisation, purity). The statements of the sections that carry them are not verified here. (5) (c)'s field-transfer lemma gives its key degree-constancy step with alternative justifications ('or follows from constancy of its Euler characteristic') and is compressed. (6) (e) claims an 'affirmative solution' of a conjecture whose form the text does not state.; conditional on: (a) cites from (d), without proving them: special termination for generalized dlt pairs in dimension four (its Theorem 11.3), relative continuation and finite runs (Propositions 9.7 and 9.9), exact extraction (Proposition 9.11), crepant gdlt modification (Proposition 11.4), and low places (Lemma 4.2(i)). It cites from (b): the common-model construction (Proposition 2.1), analytic negativity (Lemma 2.2) and terminal smoothness in codimension two (Lemma 2.3). Its difficulty and branch steps follow the projective methods of ProjectiveLCFourfolds, the companion (c), at Section 3 Proposition 3.4, Definition 4.2, Lemma 4.3, Section 5 Lemma 5.2, Section 6.1 and Section 7, with analytic steps supplied. (b) relies on Wang's analytic negativity lemma (external), and on (e)'s Lemma 2.3(i), Lemma 4.4 and Section 4.1. (d) relies on (a)'s Theorem 1.1 to exclude infinite flip tails, through its Corollary repair:cor:existing, and on its own relative and special-termination sections. (c) relies only on published inputs listed in its introduction: cone and contraction theorems, BCHM, Birkar's lc flip and complemented-pair existence results, surface mld ACC, dlt special termination, and Hodge theory. Its endpoint consequences (semiampleness, complements, Cartier sections) use three OpenAI companion preprints that are not part of its termination claim. (e) relies on Hacon and Xie (arXiv:2607.24986, July 2026) for the contractions and for finiteness of marked models away from scaling parameter zero, on Birkar (2009) for the limiting-model strategy, and on Matsumura and Zhong.
events.direction: proves termination of flip sequences in dimension four for the stated classes, answering no there only; (e) proves only existence of one finite program

A search extract described Kawamata's 2003 dimension-4 log-flip paper as claiming there is no infinite chain of log flips in dimension 4. The arXiv page shows the paper withdrawn for an error in Lemma 3.5, so the claim is not one the literature stands on.

summary: Wikipedia's Flip article (fetched; footer shows last edit 3 June 2026) says termination, that no infinite sequence of flips occurs, is open 'in dimensions greater than 3', and its footnote states the conjecture for flips of klt varieties projective over a fixed normal variety. Before 2024, dimension-4 termination is known only in restricted classes: canonical pairs (Fujino 2003, corrected by a 2004 addendum after the weighted difficulty was found wrong), klt pairs with -(K+D) numerically effective (Alexeev-Hacon-Kawamata 2006), klt pairs with Kodaira dimension at least 2 (Birkar 2008), pseudo-effective log canonical pairs (Moraga 2018), and pseudo-effective NQC generalized pairs (Chen-Tsakanikas 2020). Kawamata's 2003 dimension-4 log-flip paper was withdrawn. Conditional reductions include Birkar 2005, Moraga 2021, Hacon-Moraga 2018, and Han-Liu (2022, published 2025), the last reducing dimension-4 termination to ACC for minimal log discrepancies of enc pairs and giving an unconditional dimension-3 proof. Lazić-Xie (2023, revised to 2025) show one terminating sequence of flips for pseudo-effective projective pairs gives all flips, conditional on a Nakayama-Zariski conjecture. Inside the window: Kim (May 2024) proves termination of flips with scaling under bounded Cartier index and kappa_sigma >= dim X - 1, in any dimension; Yang-Ye-Zhang (Aug 2024) prove termination in dimension 3 only; Han-Liu-Zhuang (Sep 2025) prove every MMP terminates for projective klt 5-folds with big K+Delta or big Delta, and state that the general fivefold case is open; Hacon-Xie (Jul 2026) prove the MMP for big generalized klt Kähler pairs, with no termination claim visible in the abstract. The 2026 OpenAI manuscripts are the only results I found proving termination in dimension 4 for classes beyond the earlier ones: projective log canonical fourfolds with rational boundary, with no pseudo-effectivity or Q-factoriality (24 Sep 2026; I read the abstract, main theorem and introduction, not the proof sections in which 'permitted' programs are defined), and generalized log canonical flips on normal Q-factorial compact Kähler fourfolds with the existence of the flip diagrams assumed (7 Oct 2026; I read the full abstract and proof text, which relies on two further unrefereed OpenAI companion manuscripts). The canonical Kähler manuscript of 6 Oct 2026 and its companion 'Finite ordinary minimal model programs on compact Kähler fourfolds' were not read. All OpenAI manuscripts are attributed in the release README to 'an unreleased internal OpenAI model'; the README says the vast majority of results used one procedure with that model, and its named exceptions do not include the flip manuscripts, so the AI attribution for these is an inference from the README rather than a per-manuscript statement. I found no Lean formalization of these manuscripts (the manifest lists two Kähler entries, neither about flips, and records review status as unchecked), no review or comment by any named human expert on them (I searched for Hacon, Moraga, Fujino, Han, Liu and Lazić reactions), no later citing work, and three withdrawals from the same release on 7 Oct 2026 for a sign error in a Weil-classes argument, which is not MMP work. The ProofAtlas collaboration page for 'Termination of Flips in Arbitrary Dimension' (checked 14 Aug 2026) still lists the problem as open and names no AI system. Other AI results I checked are not about flips: AlphaProof Nexus (arXiv 2605.22763) solved Hilbert-function and Zanello log-concavity problems; Aletheia (arXiv 2602.10177) and AxiomProver are on other problems; OpenAI's Astra ten advances (Aug 2026) do not include a flip result by any source I could read. Close calls: (a) whether a dimension-4 result, or a dimension-5 general-type result, counts toward a bullet asking about every dimension above 3; (b) whether the 2026 Kähler generalized-lc manuscript's class (generalized pairs, compact Kähler, existence of flips assumed) is the same problem as the bullet's klt or projective wording; (c) whether the 'competing' Han-Liu-Zhuang dimension-5 statement, which covers only big boundary cases, should count as a case of the bullet.
competing_reading: Read as a case-by-case answer, the 2026 OpenAI results settle termination in dimension 4 for projective log canonical fourfolds with rational boundary and for generalized log canonical flips on compact Kähler fourfolds, so the bullet's answer is 'no' in dimension 4 for those classes, and the first AI-produced settlement of part of this problem is a dimension-4 result. Against that: the bullet asks about every dimension above 3, so any single-dimension result leaves all higher dimensions open, and dimension 4 was already partly known (Fujino, Alexeev-Hacon-Kawamata, Birkar, Moraga, Chen-Tsakanikas), so the 2026 manuscripts extend known cases rather than starting the question. The Kähler result also assumes the existence of the flip diagrams, which the bullet does not assume. And nothing in the record yet shows the 2026 proofs have been checked by anyone outside OpenAI.
what_would_settle_it: (1) An expert reading of the 24 Sep 2026 projective lc manuscript (including its definition of 'permitted' programs and its proof sections, which I did not read) and of the 7 Oct 2026 Kähler manuscript together with its two companion manuscripts (KahlerAuxiliary and ProjectiveLCFourfolds), plus the 6 Oct 2026 canonical Kähler manuscript (not read) and the 'Finite ordinary MMP' manuscript (not read). (2) A public verification statement, Lean formalization, or a published version of any of these. (3) An explicit answer, from any source, for termination of flips in dimension 5 or higher for arbitrary klt or lc pairs; none found, and Han-Liu-Zhuang say the general fivefold case is open. (4) A statement by the authors of Moraga 2018, Fujino, or Han-Liu on whether the 2026 results overlap or contradict their work.

event.what_happened: Donghyeon Kim (Yonsei), 'On diminished multiplier ideal and the termination of flips', arXiv 2405.11902 (v1 20 May 2024; v2 21 May 2024; v3 1 Jul 2024; v4 2 Apr 2025, 'major revision on Section 3'). Abstract (opened): proves 'a result regarding the termination of certain type of flips with scaling of an ample divisor', if the Cartier index is bounded and kappa_sigma(K_X+Delta) >= dim X - 1; extends diminished multiplier ideals to singular varieties.
event.delivers: Termination of a class of flips with scaling of an ample divisor, under two hypotheses: bounded Cartier index and kappa_sigma(K_X+Delta) >= dim X - 1. The abstract states the result for arbitrary dim X and is not unconditional.
event.remains: Flips without scaling; flips violating either hypothesis; termination of all flips in any dimension.
event.direction: Termination in a restricted class (flips with scaling, under hypotheses); cuts toward the expected answer for that class.

judgement.why: The statement asks about every dimension above 3, so any termination result for a class of pairs in dimension 4 or 5 (or under hypotheses in all dimensions, as Kim) is a case, never whole. Conditional reductions to unproven conjectures (Birkar 2005, Hacon-Moraga, Moraga 2021, Han-Liu, Lazić-Xie) and MMP results without termination claims (Das-Hacon-Paun, Hacon-Xie) are none; Yang-Ye-Zhang is dimension 3 in positive characteristic, a variant. Kawamata 2003 is withdrawn and Fujino 2003 superseded by the author's admission of errors, both knocked_down.
